# equatags

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R build status](https://github.com/ardata-fr/equatags/workflows/R-CMD-check/badge.svg)](https://github.com/ardata-fr/equatags/actions)
<!-- badges: end -->

'equatags' transforms LaTeX math expressions:

- into `HTML` and into `Office Open XML Math`, the format of equations in
  Word and PowerPoint documents, with `transform_mathjax()`;
- into sizes and drawings: `equation_size()` computes the width, height and
  depth of equations and `equation_grob()` draws them with 'grid'.

## Installation

You can install the released version from CRAN:

``` r
install.packages("equatags")
```

or the development version from GitHub:

``` r
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("ardata-fr/equatags")
```

## Office Open XML Math and HTML

```{r}
cat(transform_mathjax("x^2", to = "mml"))
```

With `to = "html"`, the result is the HTML of 'KaTeX', to be displayed with
its CSS. The 'Office Open XML Math' output can be inserted in Word documents
with the package 'officer' (or 'flextable'); see the argument `rpr` of
`transform_mathjax()` to set the size or the colour of equations.

## Size and drawing of equations

Equations are laid out with the rules of TeX and the parameters of the
'MATH' table of an OpenType math font. The default font is 'STIX Two Math',
shipped with 'gdtools': the results only depend on this file, not on the
graphic device or the machine.

```{r}
equation_size(
  c("\\frac{a+b}{c}", "\\sum_{i=1}^{n} x_i^2", "\\sqrt{x^2 + y^2}"),
  size = 12, display = TRUE
)
```

`equation_grob()` draws an equation with 'grid' (R >= 4.3), with the size
computed:

```{r grob, fig.width = 4, fig.height = 1, out.width = "60%", dpi = 150}
library(grid)
grid.newpage()
grid.draw(
  equation_grob(
    "f(x) = \\frac{1}{\\sigma\\sqrt{2\\pi}} e^{-\\frac{(x-\\mu)^2}{2\\sigma^2}}",
    size = 16, display = TRUE
  )
)
```

## Example with flextable

'flextable' uses 'equatags' to write equations in HTML, Word and PowerPoint
outputs, and to compute their sizes (`autofit()`, `gen_grob()`).

```{r eval=FALSE}
library(flextable)

eqs <- c(
  "(ax^2 + bx + c = 0)",
  "a \\ne 0",
  "x = {-b \\pm \\sqrt{b^2-4ac} \\over 2a}")
df <- data.frame(formula = eqs)

ft <- flextable(df)
ft <- mk_par(
  x = ft, j = "formula",
  value = as_paragraph(as_equation(formula)))
ft <- align(ft, align = "center", part = "all")
ft <- autofit(ft)
ft
```

## Related work

- Packages [texPreview](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=texPreview) written by 
Jonathan Sidi, "compile snippets of 'LaTeX' directly into 
images from the R console to view in the 'RStudio' viewer pane, Shiny apps 
and 'RMarkdown' documents". With this package, you can get images from 
your 'latex' code. The tool offers a wider functional spectrum than just 
equation processing and focuses on 'latex' instead of only 'MathJax' equations.

- Package [mathjaxr](https://cran.r-project.org/package=mathjaxr) written by 
Wolfgang Viechtbauer, "Using 'Mathjax' in Rd Files". This package let you 
add equations in the manual pages of your package in a very convenient way. 

- Package [katex](https://cran.r-project.org/package=katex) written by 
Jeroen Ooms, "Rendering Math to HTML, 'MathML', or R-Documentation Format". 
'equatags' mainly uses its functions.
